documents.title: University Guidelines for AI Use in the Classroom (provost announcement)
documents.summary: Provost announcement (Dec 2025) of non-binding university guidelines on AI in teaching. Faculty keep full discretion, use a green/yellow/red traffic-light model, and are asked to state expectations in syllabi. Only the announcement was retrievable, not the full guidelines.
documents.stance_why: The document says "these guidelines are not a policy" and "Faculty retain full discretion to determine whether, how, and when AI tools are used", and offers a traffic-light model of "permissible, limited, or prohibited uses", so it sets no stance itself and lists tiers.

units.why: The announcement says the guidelines were "developed through broad consultation between faculty and staff", describing how the guidance was made; P84 fits, not P56, because it reports process rather than principles.
units.anchor: developed through broad consultation between faculty and staff

units.why: The guidelines "reflect emerging best practices and examples from peer institutions", which shows benchmarking against peers; P88 fits, while the consultation clause was coded separately as P84.
units.anchor: reflect emerging best practices and examples from peer institutions

units.why: "these guidelines are not a policy" and exist to "support faculty decision making" through "a shared framework"; this is an institution-level framework statement, so P56, with actor admin and modality informs.
units.anchor: these guidelines are not a policy
units.frag_end: navigating the use of AI in teaching and learning.
units.policy: The guidelines are not a policy but a shared framework to support faculty decision making and to navigate the use of AI in teaching and learning.

units.why: "Faculty retain full discretion to determine whether, how, and when AI tools are used in their courses" hands the AI decision to each instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: Faculty retain full discretion to determine whether, how, and when AI tools are used

units.why: "Because instructional approaches and disciplinary contexts vary widely" is the reason given for issuing guidelines instead of a policy; no type covers this justification for non-uniformity, so UNCOVERED rather than stretching P04 or P83.
units.anchor: instructional approaches and disciplinary contexts vary widely
units.uncovered_note: Explains that the university gives no uniform rule because teaching approaches and disciplines differ widely.

units.why: "We ask only that instructors clearly communicate their expectations regarding AI use in course syllabi" asks every instructor to state AI expectations in the syllabus; P09 with modality should because it is phrased as a request.
units.anchor: instructors clearly communicate their expectations regarding AI use in course syllabi
units.frag_start: We ask only that instructors clearly

units.why: The guidelines "feature the "traffic light" model (green, yellow, red)" to express "permissible, limited, or prohibited uses", a named tier scheme, so P05.
units.anchor: traffic light" model (green, yellow, red)
units.policy: The guidelines feature the "traffic light" model (green, yellow, red) to help instructors articulate permissible, limited, or prohibited uses of AI tools, particularly generative AI tools, within individual courses.

units.why: The tiers are applied "within individual courses", so each course sets its own colour; this partly fits P11 (course policy governs only that course) but does not say permissions do not carry over.
units.anchor: within individual courses
units.fit_note: Says tiers are used within individual courses; does not explicitly say one course's rule does not carry over.

units.why: The principle "Faculty should clearly define expectations for AI use in assignments so students understand what is permitted" asks faculty to set expectations at assignment level; P09 fits, not P36, because it does not itself classify misuse.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly define expectations for AI use in assignments

units.why: The same sentence ties expectations to "what constitutes academic dishonesty", implying use outside the set expectations is a matter for academic integrity; P36 fits only partly.
units.anchor: what constitutes academic dishonesty
units.fit_note: Only implies that unpermitted use is dishonesty by linking it to defined expectations; no explicit classification.

units.why: The principle "Faculty retain the autonomy to align AI use with course learning objectives and disciplinary norms" makes learning objectives the basis of AI decisions, so P83.
units.anchor: align AI use with course learning objectives and disciplinary norms

units.why: "using the traffic light model as a decision support tool" frames the tiers as an optional aid, not a mandate; P05 fits with that nuance.
units.anchor: using the traffic light model as a decision support tool
units.fit_note: Stresses the tier model is a decision aid, not required.

units.why: "All users are expected to engage with AI tools ethically, with attention to ... institutional policies" sets a general expectation of ethical use under existing policy; P77 fits, with privacy and IP coded separately.
units.anchor: All users are expected to engage with AI tools ethically
units.fit_note: Mainly an ethics expectation; the reference to institutional policies is brief.

units.why: The same principle asks for "attention to data privacy", a privacy concern about AI use; P50 fits partly since it names no specific data rule.
units.anchor: attention to data privacy
units.fit_note: Only names data privacy; gives no specific data rule.

units.why: The principle also asks for attention to "intellectual property", which P52 covers; the fit is partial as nothing specific is said.
units.anchor: intellectual property
units.fit_note: Only names intellectual property without specifics.

units.why: The action item "Include a clear statement on AI use for the upcoming term" asks instructors to put an AI statement in the syllabus; P09.
units.anchor: Include a clear statement on AI use for the upcoming term

units.why: "Sample language and templates are provided in the guidelines document" supports instructors in writing statements; the nearest type is P63 (support faculty), though support here is templates only.
units.anchor: Sample language and templates are provided in the guidelines document
units.fit_note: Support is templates and sample language, not workshops or consultation.

units.why: "We welcome ongoing feedback as questions, concerns, and effective practices emerge" invites feedback on the guidelines, which P54 covers.
units.anchor: We welcome ongoing feedback as questions, concerns, and effective practices emerge

units.why: Feedback is directed to two named people, identifying who maintains the guidelines; P80 fits partly because they are contacts rather than an enforcing office.
units.anchor: Feedback can be sent to
units.policy: Feedback on the guidelines can be sent to Crystal Williams and Kyle Pokorny.
units.fit_note: Names feedback contacts, not an enforcing or exception-granting office.

units.why: "These guidelines are a starting point and we will continue to update them based on technological advancements and community feedback" commits to revising the guidance, so P54.
units.anchor: we will continue to update them based on technological advancements and community feedback

units.why: The guidelines include "links to resources ... including how other universities have handled this challenge", pointing faculty to peer examples; P88 (benchmarking against peers) fits partly.
units.anchor: how other universities have handled this challenge
units.frag_start: we are also sharing links to
units.fit_note: Shares peer examples as resources for faculty rather than forming coalitions.

units.why: The guidelines cover AI "in the classroom and in academic administration", which sets their scope; P61 fits partly since no definition of AI is given.
units.anchor: in the classroom and in academic administration
units.frag_start: UMBC's guidelines for the use of
units.fit_note: States scope only; no definition of AI.

notes: Only the provost announcement text was available; the full guidelines file is behind login, so units rely on announcement wording.
